title: Idempotency
subtitle: Give each request a key so a retry returns the first result instead of charging twice
motto: Do it once, no matter how many times you are asked
keyInsight: Retries are only safe if repeating a request changes nothing, which needs a key the server claims atomically and remembers for as long as clients might retry.

decisions.title: Start from the double charge
decisions.description: The first frame shows retries without a key charging customers twice, in dollars, so the pattern is motivated by a cost.
decisions.alternatives: Starting from the definition of idempotence would not show why retries make it matter.

decisions.title: Include the check-then-write race
decisions.description: The failure frame lets some retries overlap the first attempt, since a key that is read and then written in two steps still lets duplicates through.
decisions.alternatives: Showing only a key that works would hide that the claim has to be one atomic step.
